NSAIDs may reduce renal function, monitor metformin accumulation risk and potential for lactic acidosis.
No significant interaction known. Safe to use together.
Aspirin may reduce the antihypertensive effect of ACE inhibitors. Monitor blood pressure closely.

Omeprazole may slightly increase metformin levels. Monitor for hypoglycemia.
PPIs may decrease levothyroxine absorption. Take levothyroxine 4 hours before omeprazole.
Combined use may cause excessive blood pressure lowering and bradycardia. Monitor vital signs.
No significant interaction. Safe to use together.
SSRIs with aspirin increase bleeding risk. Monitor for bruising, bleeding, or gastrointestinal symptoms.
SSRIs combined with NSAIDs significantly increase bleeding risk, especially GI bleeding.
Often prescribed together. No significant adverse interaction. Monitor potassium and blood pressure.

Thiazides may impair glucose control. Monitor blood glucose more frequently.
Sertraline may increase levothyroxine requirements. Monitor TSH levels.
